items.title: Introducing harness adapters: adapt your favorite model to your harness to improve performance and cost
items.summary_1line: Hugging Face describes training a LoRA harness adapter with RL on Qwen3.8-27B, reporting Terminal-Bench 2.1 pass@1 rising from 39% to 55% with the Pi harness while average token use drops from 2.9K to 1.5K.
items.editor_note: 출발점: 하니스 적합성을 학습 가능한 속성으로 보며, 토큰은 절반만 쓰고 Terminal-Bench에서 16포인트 향상을 달성했다.

items.title: Jcode: High performance coding agent harness written in Rust
items.summary_1line: Jcode is an open-source coding agent harness that runs multiple agents in parallel on the same repo, with a server that notifies agents of file changes and manages messaging and swarm coordination.
items.editor_note: 레버를 학습에서 오케스트레이션으로 옮긴다. 병렬 에이전트들이 조율 서버를 통해 하나의 저장소를 공유한다.

items.title: Delegent: A Multi-Agent Harness That Reduces Cost without Sacrificing Performance
items.summary_1line: Delegent is an agent harness built on Claude Code that keeps a frontier model in charge while handing easy subtasks to a small local model, cutting frontier cost by 67% on long-horizon coding and 59% on agentic search.
items.why_it_matters: Matches feed focus: agentic, harness, claude code.
items.editor_note: 모델 라우팅을 세 번째 레버로 추가했으며, 이 스레드에서 보고된 비용 절감폭이 가장 크다.

editorial.tldr: Hugging Face opened the thread on Nov 20 by training a LoRA adapter that fits a model to its harness, raising Qwen3.8-27B's Terminal-Bench 2.1 pass@1 from 39% to 55% on half the tokens. On Nov 23 Jcode, an open-source Rust harness, shifted the lever to running parallel agents on one repo with a server that coordinates file changes.
editorial.whats_new: Delegent, an arXiv harness built on Claude Code, keeps a frontier model in charge and hands easy subtasks to a small local model, reporting 67% lower frontier cost on long-horizon coding and 59% on agentic search.
editorial.why_it_matters: Three separate teams treat the harness, not the model, as the tuning surface for agent cost and pass rate: adapter training, parallel orchestration, and frontier-to-local delegation.
editorial.take_for_builders: Before switching models to cut agent cost, benchmark harness changes on your own tasks: log frontier-token spend per subtask and test routing the cheap ones to a local model.

status.detail: Each result is self-reported by its authors on its own benchmark; no item yet compares the three approaches on a shared task.

beats.summary: A coordinating server notifies agents of file changes and handles messaging between them; no benchmark numbers attached.

open_questions: Does a harness adapter trained for Pi keep its Terminal-Bench gain when the same model runs in a different harness?
Does Delegent's frontier-cost cut hold once local-model latency and hardware cost are counted?
Does Jcode publish pass-rate or throughput numbers against a single-agent harness?
Does any independent group reproduce these gains on a shared benchmark such as Terminal-Bench?
